title: Introduce semantically-balanced probe and CI noise suppressor for prompt-set regression checks
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: Current prompt-set regression checks sample uniformly from test pools and often underrepresent semantically rare but important cohorts. This PR introduces a semantically-balanced probe that samples prompts proportional to cluster rarity (via embedding clusters) and a CI-side suppressor that reduces noisy flakiness alerts from low-confidence cohorts. The goal is to improve signal-to-noise in CI alerts while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What this PR does: Adds a new probe (sem_balance_probe) and a CI adapter hook (noise_suppressor) that together provide: 1) embedding-based clustering of prompt sets with configurable cluster granularity; 2) stratified sampling so each CI run includes a fixed quota from each cluster, with oversampling of rare clusters; 3) a dynamic quorum scoring mechanism that requires multiple independent failure modes (semantic cluster-level Delta + per-prompt regression) before raising a hard CI failure; 4) an adaptive suppressor that converts low-confidence cluster blips into soft alerts with an explanatory tag and a suggested backfill command for escalation; 5) telemetry hooks to surface cohort-level metrics in Redwood Console.

Implementation notes: The probe uses existing sentence-transformer embeddings from eval-harness, then applies mini-batch k-means with an autoscale option keyed to prompt-set size. The cluster IDs are cached and pinned per test run via a small metadata blob stored alongside the prompt-set snapshot to ensure determinism across reruns. Quorum scoring is computed as a weighted sum of (cluster-level mean delta, proportion of prompts in cluster failing threshold, historical volatility) with tunable thresholds via config. The suppressor includes a whitelist for high-priority prompt tags and an opt-out label for teams that want strict fail-fast behavior.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for clustering edge cases and deterministic caching. Integration smoke runs against three internal prompt-sets (chat-assistant, summarization, rerank) with synthetic regressions injected to validate quorum behavior. CI matrix includes python 3.10 and 3.11 runners. Performance: end-to-end probe adds ~1.2s overhead per 1000 prompt-set entries when embeddings are cached; initial runs show a 38% reduction in flaky CI failures (measured on historical CI flake corpus).

Things to watch / follow-ups: 1) Backfill job to recompute clusters for large historical prompt archives (tracked in linked_linear ENG-9412). 2) UX: expose cluster breakdown and suppressor decisions in the eval report UI (follow-up PR planned). 3) Investigate replacing k-means with hierarchical clustering for very long-tail prompt distributions.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration smoke runs - [x] Metrics emitted to telemetry - [x] Docs snippet in ci-hooks.md - [x] Reviewed and approved by reviewers

Related: This complements existing cohort and drift detectors but focuses on sampling strategy and suppressing transient noise rather than detecting trend drift.
